title: What Is AI Detector Interoperability and Why Does It Matter for Governance?
hook_questions: How do independent AI detectors verify each other's outputs?
What happens when two certified AI auditors disagree on the same model?
Why is cross-detector calibration essential for regulatory enforcement?
answer_summary: AI detector interoperability ensures that independent evaluation tools produce consistent, comparable results when assessing the same AI system. Without it, two regulators using different detectors could reach opposite conclusions about the same model compliance. The Council of AI framework addresses this through standardized measurement protocols, cross-detector calibration benchmarks, and cryptographic verification chains that make detector disagreement auditable rather than ambiguous.
regulatory_context: As jurisdictions adopt mandatory AI auditing (EU AI Act Art 26-29, Colorado SB 205, NYC Local Law 144), the question of detector equivalence becomes legally load-bearing. The ISO/IEC 42006 audit standard and NIST AI 600-1 profile both reference the need for measurement reproducibility across tools.
council_position: Monitored containment, not provable isolation. Verified measurement credential with cross-detector coherence audit trail.
